/staticQuestions/0/answer.source_en: All three share ⟦G1⟧ + ⟦G0⟧ + Starfield Library. This version adds ⟦G2⟧ in Yongin (Buddhist, 3,000+ statues, world's largest wooden reclining Buddha). The Folk Village version adds Korean Folk Village (270+ traditional houses, K-drama filming). The Gwangmyeong version adds the underground LED-lit cave park. Pick this one if Buddhist sculpture interests you most; the Folk Village version for deepest heritage; Gwangmyeong for variety and indoor weather.

/staticQuestions/0/question.source_en: How is this different from the Suwon + Folk Village or Suwon + ⟦G0⟧ tours?

/staticQuestions/1/answer.source_en: Yes — all three paid stops are included: ⟦G1⟧ (1,000 KRW adult), ⟦G0⟧ (1,500 KRW adult), and ⟦G2⟧ (free admission). Starfield Library is also free for everyone. Optional café drinks, mall food hall meals, and any souvenir purchases are at your own cost.

/staticQuestions/2/answer.source_en: No. Lunch is during free time at Starfield Suwon's mall food hall — large variety, casual seating, typically 10,000-20,000 KRW per person. The library and mall are stop #2 (≈13:30 arrival) so the timing works as a natural break between Hwaseong in the morning and Waujeongsa in the afternoon.

/staticQuestions/3/answer.source_en: It's a non-traditional temple: founded in 1970 by Monk Kim Hae-Geun (a North Korean refugee) and built around a single founder's collection of 3,000+ Buddha statues from across Asia. The headline pieces are the Buldu — an 8-meter wooden Buddha head registered in the Guinness Book of Records as the world's largest — and the Wabul, a 3m × 12m wooden reclining Buddha carved from an Indonesian juniper. The 12-ton Bell of Unification was rung at the start of the 1988 Seoul Olympics. Free admission, ≈75 minutes recommended.

/staticQuestions/4/answer.source_en: Covered shoulders are recommended at Waujeongsa — bring a light layer if wearing a sleeveless top in summer. Hats are typically removed inside the main halls. No strict dress code is enforced for outdoor temple grounds, but modest clothing is appreciated as a sign of respect. Comfortable walking shoes with grip help with the temple's stairs and inclines.

/staticQuestions/4/question.source_en: Do I need to dress modestly for the temple?

/staticQuestions/5/answer.source_en: Three different walking styles: Hwaseong Fortress wall has the hardest section (steep gradients, stairs at gates, ≈1 km walked); Starfield Library is fully indoor with escalators; Waujeongsa has stairs and inclines on temple grounds (moderate). Total walking ≈3-4 km across the day. Comfortable shoes essential, especially for the wall walk and temple paths.

/staticQuestions/5/question.source_en: How is the walking load distributed across the day?

/staticQuestions/6/answer.source_en: Yes — this is one of the strongest first-time picks for travelers who want one UNESCO heritage site, one contemporary photo space, and one distinctive Buddhist temple in a single guided day. The format keeps things balanced rather than active, with all stops geographically close (Suwon-Yongin corridor, ≈30 min apart). Free hotel pickup from Hongdae or ⟦G0⟧ simplifies the morning logistics.

/staticQuestions/6/question.source_en: Is this a good choice for first-time visitors to Suwon & Yongin?

/staticQuestions/7/answer.source_en: Moderate active walking. The hardest section is Hwaseong Fortress: ≈1 km of stone wall walk with steep gradients, stairs at gates, and uneven historic surfaces — comfortable shoes with grip essential. Starfield Library is easy indoor walking on flat floors. ⟦G0⟧ has some uphill paths and stairs (moderate). Total walking ≈3-4 km across the day. Strollers difficult on the wall and temple, fine at Starfield.

/staticQuestions/8/answer.source_en: Yes — comfortable for most families with children age 6+. Strollers are challenging on the Hwaseong wall and at Waujeongsa, but Starfield is fully stroller-friendly with escalators and elevators. Kids often respond strongly to Waujeongsa's giant Buddha head and the 3,000+ statue collection. Hanbok rental at ⟦G0⟧ is a popular family photo moment (and gets free fortress admission).

/staticQuestions/8/question.source_en: Is this tour suitable for families?

/staticQuestions/9/answer.source_en: Yes for active seniors comfortable with stairs and uneven ground; more limited for low-mobility travelers. The Hwaseong wall walk has the hardest sections (steep gradients, stone steps); seniors can walk the easier flat segments and skip the climb to command posts. Waujeongsa has temple-ground stairs but the main statue collection is on accessible levels. Starfield is fully escalator/elevator-accessible — the recovery stop.

/staticQuestions/9/question.tm: Les personnes âgées peuvent-elles participer confortablement ?

/staticQuestions/10/answer.source_en: Best fit is around age 6 and up. The fortress wall has stairs and uneven historic surfaces, and Waujeongsa's temple grounds have inclines that tire very young children. Older kids do well — the giant Buddha head and the Bell of Unification have a 'wow' factor and Starfield's library is accessible. Strollers manage well at Starfield but not on the wall.
